worldcup.title: Will Spain bring more pain for Tuchel’s tired England?
worldcup.summary: Come Saturday, it will be 73 days since the pain and shame of Atlanta, when England, from a winning position in a World Cup semi-final, decided to do an England, and sit on their lead. What followed resembled a slow-motion crash test dummies video, Enzo Fernández first summoning the ghost of Andy Möller at Euro 96 with his high-camp cavorting celebration, and then Lautaro Martínez, unmarked, nodding home. Englishmen across the globe slumped, Croydon BoxPark fell deathly silent. Allowing Lionel Messi the freedom of Georgia on the inside-right channel had turned out to be a critical oversight. Whoops. As an avid Manchester United fan, I would love to have a clump of the hallowed turf on display in my living room for daily worship purposes (yesterday’s Football Daily, full email edition). However, what are the chances of my getting a piece that isn’t covered in spit and nasal blowings? I’d say highly unlikely, so I think I’d respectfully give it a miss” – Nigel Green. I wonder if Harry Kane’s desire to play in the NFL is because someone told him that as a kicker in American football every time an opposing player touched him it would be a penalty?” – Pat Condreay. Continue reading...

worldcup.title: Kieron Dyer making waves at Southend after leaving ‘hooligan’ days and ‘deathbed’ behind
worldcup.summary: Day in former England midfielder’s company reveals a chess fan and hands-on manager who will not tolerate tardiness Kieron Dyer is recounting a tale from his time in Japan at the 2002 World Cup. “You have a lot of time on your hands,” he begins from behind his desk at Southend United’s training ground. Dyer, a chess fan, was looking for an opponent in the England squad. “Sol Campbell was a deep thinker, and I asked if he played. He said yes, and I told him I’d pummel him. I’m not joking, we played for an hour and he’d moved two pieces. If that was how much he was thinking so early …” Dyer belly laughs. “I was like: ‘Sol, I’m not sitting here for five hours playing chess with you, mate!’” Continue reading...

general.summary: Australia 1-1 Brazil in international friendly in Townsville Irankunda hits free kick before Rayan equalises deep in added time It was a Friday night in which the stars descended on Townsville. There was Bruno Guimarães, Raphinha and Vinícius Júnior in the Brazilian XI, with Endrick leading the line and Estêvão out on the flank, all instructed by Carlo Ancelotti in the dugout. But on this evening, their limelight was stolen by Australia’s star boy Nestory Irankunda. His magnificent 68th-minute free kick may have been cancelled out at the death by Rayan’s header, ensuring Australia and Brazil shared a 1-1 draw at Queensland Country Bank Stadium, but on a night in which some of the planet’s biggest and best were on hand, Irankunda stood up to be counted. general.title: Pocognoli deserves time but Scottish FA must also prove its credentials
general.summary: Scotland’s unproven head coach represents a gamble made by an organisation that could do without another embarrassing episode If time is the commodity most cherished by a manager, Sébastien Pocognoli’s decision to lead Scotland is no surprise. Host nation status for Euro 2028 means it will be exceptionally difficult for them not to qualify for the tournament. In the Nations League, starting on Saturday in Slovenia, Pocognoli can experiment without fear of serious consequence. The 39-year-old has taken over a national team that represents a country which had not only – and partly unfairly – grown weary of Steve Clarke but screamed for a brave new dawn. The public wants what the public gets. They are unlikely to turn on Pocognoli, even if the start to his international management career proves bumpy. Continue reading...

general.title: Greenpeace, Avusturya'yı Avrupa Komisyonu'na şikayet etti!
general.summary: Greenpeace, Avusturya aleyhine Avrupa Komisyonu'na şikayette bulunarak, ülkenin yanıltıcı çevre iddialarına karşı yeni AB kurallarını uygulamaya koymasının Avrupa hukukunu ihlal ettiğini öne sürdü. Çevre örgütü, Avusturya'da üretilen ürünlerin, yeni AB şartlarını karşılamasa bile, çevreyle ilgili iddialarla üç yıl daha pazarlanmaya devam edebileceğini söyledi. Çevre konusunda yanıltıcı veya asılsız iddialarda bulunma uygulaması olan "yeşil yıkama" ile mücadele etmeyi amaçlayan AB'nin Tüketicileri Yeşil Geçiş İçin Güçlendirme (EmpCo) direktifi pazar günü yürürlüğe giriyor. AB, uzaya erişimde uydu talebi nedeniyle kapasite açığı yaşıyor Kurallara göre, çevresel iddiaların doğrulanabilir olması gerekirken, sürdürülebilirlik etiketlerine yalnızca sertifikasyon gereksinimlerini karşılamaları durumunda izin verilecek. Kurallar ayrıca iklim nötrlüğü iddialarına ilişkin gereksinimleri de sıkılaştırıyor. Yalnızca asgari yasal standartlara dayalı olarak çevresel faydaların reklamının yapılması, ayrıca ürünlerin dayanıklılığı ve onarılabilirliği hakkında yanıltıcı iddialarda bulunulması da yasaklanacak.

general.title: James Garner keen to live up to ‘mini-Valverde’ tag after late England call
general.summary: Everton midfielder’s spirit and intelligence earned him another chance and he is eager to test himself against Spain in the Nations League on Saturday “It’s a very good comparison,” James Garner says, and he is not kidding. It came from Thomas Tuchel in March after the England manager had watched the Everton midfielder impress on his international debut against Uruguay. He was up against Federico Valverde and Tuchel went big with his praise. Garner was a “mini Valverde”, he said after the 1-1 draw at Wembley. It was surely too much, despite the prefix that Tuchel attached, yet it was possible to see where he was coming from. Like Valverde, Garner wants to operate in central midfield but he can play at right-back or on the wing. And like Valverde, who they called El Pajarito – or the Little Bird – when he was a kid, Garner can sometimes fly a bit under the radar. Continue reading...
